summary: Wooden L-4 lookout tower in Medicine Bow NF near Esterbrook, planned for 1940, staffed 1946-1953, now listed as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; one lookout history page says removed. No removal date is given.

events.note: Summer 1940 completion planned per a June 1940 newspaper item quoted by the source; completion not separately confirmed.
Don March listed as lookout personnel, 1946-1953.
Lightning temporarily damaged the tower radio, stopping communications until repairs were made.
Final year of the 1946-1953 personnel listing.

evidence.supports: Agency is Medicine Bow National Forest; location about 20 miles south of Douglas
Location about 20 miles south of Douglas
Design 30-foot wooden L-4 tower; status gone; lookout personnel Don March 1946-1953
evidence.quote: 30' wooden L-4 tower. Gone. Known lookout personnel: 1946-1953: Don March.

evidence.supports: CCC camp to move to Esterbrook camp for summer 1940 work
evidence.quote: The CCC camp of 200 boys at Centennial, west of Laramie, will move to the Esterbrook camp, south of Douglas

evidence.supports: Summer 1940 work planned to complete a lookout tower a mile east of the ranger station
evidence.quote: Work for the summer includes completion of a lookout tower a mile east of the ranger station and completion of a telephone line to that point.

evidence.supports: August 1952 lightning temporarily damaged the Esterbrook tower radio and stopped communications
evidence.quote: Last night lightning also temporarily damaged the radio of the Esterbrook lookout tower, stopping communications until repairs had been made.

evidence.supports: Same report: Laramie Peak division had five fires in four days
evidence.quote: has burst into flames five times in the last four days

evidence.supports: One lookout history page lists the tower as removed
Wyoming directory lists the Esterbrook tower as gone

notes_for_editor: The 1940 build year is a planned summer completion from a June 1940 newspaper item quoted on westlookouts; no source confirms the finished date. The 1952 and 1940 newspaper items are second-hand quotes on the westlookouts page and were not checked against the originals. Both lookout pages say gone or removed but give no removal date, so the timeline has no fate event. No source describes the site today or its access.
